items_missed: Never asked 'how are you today?' or any warm-up — call opened 'Hello, this is Frank. How can I help you?' and went straight to 'Did you have a date in mind?'

Agenda statement was given ('I build you a profile and ask a bunch of questions about the move so I understand the scope and then we can talk a little pricing an estimate and I can email that over') but with no timeframe and no 'Sound good?' confirmation — the customer answered with three flat 'Okay's, so he never actually got a yes.

No moving-stressor question. Never asked anything like 'Is there anything you're particularly worried about with this move?' on a three-stop move where the customer was clearly managing logistics herself.

No 'pricing is super simple' opener — the transition was the flatter 'so how our pricing works, we have a two and a half hour minimum.' ('It's super simple' appeared later, but about the payment iPad, not pricing.)

Disassembly/reassembly never mentioned as included — and it was directly applicable: the customer listed 'a dresser a bed and a desk.' She was never told the crew breaks down and rebuilds the bed at no extra charge.

No Worries Damage Coverage only half-delivered: 'our damage coverage, all that stuff is just rolled in baked into the hourly rate.' Never named No Worries, never gave the up-to-$2,000 figure, never said repair, replace, or reimburse. Half credit.
Meet Your Mover never mentioned — no mention of the pre-move email with the mover's photo and info.

On-Time Guarantee never mentioned — notable because the customer specifically negotiated an early start ('do you have like an early time on the eighth that day?') and got 8:30am. That was the open door for the guarantee and it went unused.

Estimate anchored to the bottom of the range. He quoted 'between two and a half to three and a half hours' and then twice steered her down — 'you're probably falling the lower end of that range' and 'the two and a half hour range is what I would guess.' This is a three-stop move with roughly 19 miles of driving, a second-floor load, a storage drop, and a second-floor unload; guiding her to the 2.5-hour minimum is the estimate-accuracy failure mode in miniature.
Assembly/disassembly never priced into the time estimate as a variable, despite a bed and desk in the inventory.

Entire Save Your Ass prep speech missing. No 'prep before move day means a shorter move and a lower bill,' no consolidation examples (loose drawer items, photos off walls, garden tools), no 'take a carload,' no closing sense-check on prep. Partial credit only for the time-based framing ('we're just time based... what I'm trying to calculate the time' / 'you only pay for actual time used').

'No deposit required' never said. He covered payment mechanics — 'the movers will just take a credit or debit card once they stop the clock' — but never named the no-deposit differentiator, which is one of Einstein's two headline promises.
No BOLDED-details framing for the confirmation email — the customer was never told the key details would be at the top for her to verify at a glance.

Hours and how to reach us never given. This matters more than usual here: the customer committed three separate times to calling back with the storage unit number ('I'll definitely call beforehand so everybody knows where exactly where we're going') and was never told when or where to call. Frank redirected her to email reply only.

Customer's name never used during the call, and the farewell used the wrong name: 'thank you so much Lisa' to Alicia Marshall — after she had spelled it out letter by letter ('A as in apple, L-I...').

No Sparefoot referral on a call where the customer explicitly had not booked her storage unit yet ('you don't have the unit there yet, right?' / 'I will call back well before and update'). No Ecobox mention either, despite her stating 'I will be the one packing' and needing roughly 20-25 boxes.
No 60c/lb baseline valuation explanation to contrast against the damage coverage.

Storage unit details left open (floor, elevator, walk) with the resolution left entirely on the customer to call in — and Frank himself named it as the main time risk ('maybe you're on the fifth floor and the elevators tiny'). No callback commitment on his side and nothing set to chase it before Oct 8.
top_strength: The probe was the strongest part of this call and it was genuinely thorough. Frank captured all three addresses with zips, correctly caught the storage stop as a scope change on the fly ('Gotcha, alright, so we're making an additional stop to a storage'), and then worked both floors, both stair situations, parking, and walk distance with real specificity rather than generalities: 'depending on where we can park, do you know, or can you estimate, like how far the walking distance would be from where we can park our truck to your unit,' then followed up with 'what would you say? 25 feet, fifty feet, hundred feet' to force a usable number. He benchmarked box count instead of asking an open question — 'We typically see around 25 boxes for that home size. Do you think you'll have any more than that?' — and kept pushing on inventory when her answer sounded thin, 'Just three,' then 'Yeah, no, like coffee tables, TVs stools,' which surfaced a 50-inch TV she had not mentioned. He also explained why he was asking, which builds trust: 'cause we're just time based so I'm just looking to see you know, how many pieces needs to be moved.' The clock explanation was complete and clear — contract on the iPad at the door, 2.5-hour minimum, 15-minute prorated increments, only pay for time used — and he gave concrete dollar anchors ($208/hr for two movers, $520 at the minimum, $728 at three hours) instead of leaving her to do the math. He booked the job on the call.
coaching_note: Highest-leverage fix is the estimate anchor. Frank gave a defensible range and then talked her down to the floor of it twice: 'you're probably falling the lower end of that range' and 'the two and a half hour range is what I would guess.' On a job with two second-floor carries, a storage drop, and 19 miles of driving, that sets her expectation at the minimum and sets the branch up to be over on move day — the exact pattern behind the 45-46% estimate accuracy number. What he should have said, having already done the math out loud himself: 'Alicia, with the drive between three stops plus stairs on both ends, I'd plan on right around three hours, so about $624 — and if the crew beats that you only pay for the time they use.' Anchor at the realistic middle and let the customer be pleasantly surprised, never the reverse. Second priority, and it is free points on every call: the differentiators. He was handed both openings and took neither. She asked for the earliest possible start and got 8:30am — that is where On-Time Guarantee goes ('and we back that up: if we miss your window, we start discounting immediately'). She has a bed, a dresser, and a desk — that is where included disassembly and reassembly goes. And 'our damage coverage, all that stuff is just rolled in' needs to become the actual line: 'our No Worries Damage Coverage, up to $2,000 per move to repair, replace, or reimburse accidental damage, at no extra cost.' Meet Your Mover was never said at all. Third, the Save Your Ass speech is entirely absent on a call where it would have paid for itself — she is self-packing and hovering at the 2.5-hour minimum, so 'anything you can take in your own car the day before, take it — every trip the crew doesn't make comes off your bill' would have both protected the estimate and made her feel like he was on her side. Two loose ends to close in EMMA today, both operational, not coaching: (1) the storage unit is booked-but-unknown and Frank left the entire follow-up on the customer, with no hours or callback number given and no task on his side to chase it before Oct 8 — that is a load-planning gap on a stop he himself flagged as the main time risk; (2) she had not booked storage yet, which was a live Sparefoot referral he walked past. Small thing worth naming because the customer will remember it: he closed with 'thank you so much Lisa' after she spelled Alicia out letter by letter, and used her name zero times before that.
phone_presence_notes: Competent and easy to talk to, with a few genuinely natural affirmations ('That's good thinking. Actually.' when she reasoned through school traffic, and 'No, that's perfect!'), but the language was largely procedural, padded with filler ('Okay. Okay. Okay.' and 'Let me see. Let's see. Let's see. Let's see.'), carried no empathy markers on a three-stop move, used her name zero times, and closed on the wrong name.
audio_review_reason: The customer's side of the transcript is heavily ASR-garbled ('I'm Flueger mille to round rock so short kitten', 'if it did take the full $3', '8:39 start time' for what was almost certainly 8:30), so two judgment calls need audio confirmation: whether the closing 'thank you so much Lisa' was a real name error or a transcription artifact, and whether the missing agenda confirmation and warmth markers reflect tone or just a lossy transcript.
